correctness.rationale: The continuous endpoint mass of one transformed component is a/(2πc); its Poisson kernel has ratio q=(a-c)/(a+c). Averaging the absolutely convergent Fourier series retains precisely the multiples of n and gives the stated mass. For odd n both q→q^n and x→(1+x)/(1-x) are strictly increasing, and q_i strictly decreases with c; the extreme component scales bracket the root, including the all-equal case. For n=2m the displayed second derivative factors into nonnegative factors times the bracket (2m-1)(1+R^m)-2 sum_{j=1}^{m-1}R^j, which is at least m(1+R^m) by the secant bound for R^j (including R=0 by continuity). Curvature can vanish only at isolated points, and mass diverges at both log-scale ends, giving strict convexity and a unique minimizer. In the balanced two-scale case reflection fixes the even minimum at g=√(ab). The odd root has s=log(c/g)>0 and obeys (u/v)^n=1-2u^n for 0<u≤r≤v<1. Taking logs gives n(log v-log u)=O(r^n), so s=O(r^n/n) by the positive derivative of log(v/u). Consequently u^n is asymptotic to r^n and the derivative at zero is (1-r^2)/r, giving the claimed coefficient. Finite independent checks found direct-grid/formula agreement within 6.33e-81, and odd displacement ratios tending to 1 (0.999650183 at n=5 and 0.9999999965 at n=13 for scales 1,9).
residual_risks: The independent replay is bounded and is not a proof of the all-parameter statement or an assessment of finite-precision conditioning.
